standard_prerequisites.name: Fraisse limits and nonarchimedean permutation topology
standard_prerequisites.statement: Existence, uniqueness, universality and ultrahomogeneity of the Fraisse limit of finite ordered Delta-metric spaces; basic open pointwise stabilizers; open subgroups are closed; conjugacy of finite stabilizers under the action.

standard_prerequisites.name: Explicit classical extension and displacement inputs
standard_prerequisites.statement: Slutsky Theorem4.12 and ordered Remark4.13, exactly as quoted at653-663, provide simultaneous extensions of two order-preserving partial isometries and a free-amalgam word, with distances in the generated additive semigroup. Neumann finite-set displacement lemma applies when all subgroup orbits are infinite. These are explicit imported reference theorems; the alternating order-propagation and group reconstruction remain local obligations.

core_obligations: Starting with the supplied free-amalgam word, build successive ordered copies and alternating A- and B-fixing partial isometries to move all new points into the necessary order gaps; cap distances at sup Delta and extend the resulting conjugation word to approximate any finite target automorphism.
Use dense generation by disjoint stabilizers and the finite-orbit argument to characterize point stabilizers intrinsically as maximal proper closed subgroups that are open.
Reconstruct points from their stabilizers, recover equality of pair distances by conjugacy of intersections, and turn the induced distance bijection into a triangle-preserving equivalence.
difficulty_reason: Even with the explicit previously published Slutsky extension theorem and standard Fraisse/Neumann inputs, the ordered propagation by alternating stabilizers and the ensuing topological-group reconstruction are substantial. The theorem is distinct from numerical rigidity or coding of distance sets and is not a direct use of a generic reconstruction theorem.

compared.difference: Public theorem fixes normalized unbounded distance sets from their triangle relation; it does not reconstruct any group or action.
Prepared coding theorem converts linear-order isomorphism into bounded triangle equivalence, with no stabilizer reconstruction.
Prepared dense-set theorem identifies triangle bijections as scalings, not ordered automorphism groups.

Credited predecessor supplies the proof outline, but the ordered stabilizer-density propagation670-776 is explicitly proved locally. The imported theorem is not used as a black box for the ordered implication.
